title: The neocloud refinancing wall (2026-2028) - CoreWeave/Oracle debt schedules meet the Fed hike
source: Public record: CoreWeave Q2 2026 disclosures (contractual maturities, interest expense); Oracle FY2026 10-K + Q1 FY2027 10-Q; Motley Fool/Capacity/DCD/HSBC. Structural overlay (no financial-core edges; dollar figures in notes). HONESTY: CoreWeave's year-by-year schedule + interest expense = fact from filings; Oracle's aggregate debt + interest = fact, but its year-by-year maturity table was NOT reliably available (grade); analyst shortfall/rate estimates = reported.

edges.notes: CoreWeave Q2-2026: total debt ~$35.1B vs ~$5.0B equity + ~$6.9B cash; contractual principal $4.4B (rest-2026), $6.2B (2027, the key hurdle), $4.4B (2028), then $14.9B post-2030. Quarterly interest ~$640M (2.4x YoY); rates span converts ~2% / senior notes ~10% / oldest DDTL ~15% / new $2.6B facility SOFR+550bps (2031). Ba3/B+ high-yield; HSBC flagged a ~$8.9B 2026 liquidity shortfall (fact from filings; shortfall = analyst estimate).

Oracle total borrowings ~$129.5B (May 2026, up from ~$92.6B); raised ~$43B debt + $5B equity FY2026, plans ~$40B FY2027 (incl a $20B ATM), no new debt in CY2026; Q1-FY2027 interest expense $1.428B (+55% YoY). Year-by-year maturity table not reliably public here - staggered, some decades out (aggregate = fact; per-year schedule = graded, verify in 10-K).

Nebius (~$8.5B debt) is the third leg of the Oracle/CoreWeave/Nebius trio whose combined ~$152B planned capex vs ~$106B revenue + ~7.8x debt/quarterly-revenue leverage defines the neocloud stress (fact of category; figures reported).

The wall concentrates neocloud + hyperscaler-SPV maturities into a tightening 2026-2028 window - a refinancing TEST (roll at higher rates or contract), the leveraged edge of the map's SINK/bond thread (fact of window; test framing interpretation).

Timing collision: the Sep-2026 Fed hike (to 3.75-4.00%, another possible) raises refinancing cost RIGHT as the wall arrives - floating-rate facilities reprice up and new issues price off higher Treasuries, worsening the roll (fact-of-direction; cross-link to spec-fed-hike-2026).

The wall is the debt-service counterpart to the AI-capex buildout: GPUs financed short/expensive against fast-depreciating collateral, with revenue concentrated in a few (unrated) anchor customers (e.g. Anthropic ~40% of one CoreWeave loan) - the depreciation/duration-mismatch trap made concrete (fact of structure; trap framing interpretation).

Much of the wall is held by private-credit funds (Blackstone/Blue Owl/Apollo/Pimco/BlackRock, per spec-ai-datacenter-debt-spv) - so a failed roll transmits into their portfolios, not just the borrowers' (fact of holders; contagion path interpretation).
